victims.name: Tsar Nicholas II
victims.description: The last Emperor of Russia. Regal, doomed, and probably regretting several personnel decisions.

comments.rasputin: Rasputin was closely associated with Nicholas II's imperial family.
comments.napoleon: Another emperor. Napoleon presumably considers that sufficient justification.

victims.name: Tsarina Alexandra
victims.description: Empress of Russia and a devoted believer in Rasputin's abilities.

comments.rasputin: Alexandra's trust in Rasputin helped give him extraordinary access to the imperial family.

victims.name: Prince Felix Yusupov
victims.description: Russian aristocrat, fabulously wealthy, and experienced in extremely complicated murder plots.

comments.rasputin: Yusupov participated in Rasputin's actual murder. Apparently Rasputin has objected.

victims.name: Manderup Parsberg
victims.description: Danish nobleman remembered primarily for one exceptionally consequential argument.

comments.brahe: Brahe dueled Parsberg in 1566. The encounter cost Brahe part of his nose.

victims.name: Johannes Kepler
victims.description: Astronomer, mathematician, planetary-motion enthusiast, and inheritor of some very valuable observations.

comments.brahe: Kepler worked with Brahe and gained access to his astronomical observations after Brahe's death.

victims.name: Galileo Galilei
victims.description: Astronomer, physicist, telescope enthusiast, and accomplished professional troublemaker.

comments.brahe: A rival astronomical worldview is more than enough motive in this institution.

victims.name: Isaac Newton
victims.description: Mathematician, physicist, alchemist, and notoriously unpleasant coworker.

comments.brahe: Newton arrived later, but chronology has never stopped an academic dispute here.
comments.curie: Physics eventually became Curie's territory too. The centuries are irrelevant.

victims.name: Charles Babbage
victims.description: Designer of enormous mechanical computers he had considerable difficulty actually finishing.

comments.lovelace: Lovelace's work on Babbage's Analytical Engine produced her most famous contributions to computing.

victims.name: Lord Byron
victims.description: Romantic poet, celebrity scandal generator, and apparently inexhaustible source of bad decisions.

comments.lovelace: Byron was Ada Lovelace's father, though she barely knew him.
comments.crowley: There is no important historical connection. Crowley presumably found one anyway.

victims.name: Augustus De Morgan
victims.description: Mathematician and logician who would eventually have laws named after him.

comments.lovelace: De Morgan tutored Lovelace in mathematics.

victims.name: Alan Turing
victims.description: Mathematician, cryptanalyst, computing pioneer, and a man born roughly a century too late for this argument.

comments.lovelace: Both became foundational figures in computing. Chronology has been overruled.

victims.name: Arthur Edward Waite
victims.description: Occultist, mystic, writer, and participant in organizations where nobody could simply get along.

comments.crowley: Waite and Crowley were bitter occult rivals. Crowley repeatedly mocked him in print.

victims.name: William Butler Yeats
victims.description: Poet, Nobel laureate, occultist, and unwilling participant in magical organizational politics.

comments.crowley: Yeats and Crowley were rivals within the Hermetic Order of the Golden Dawn.

victims.name: Samuel Liddell MacGregor Mathers
victims.description: Occultist, ceremonial magician, and proof that even secret magical societies need office politics.

comments.crowley: Mathers was Crowley's mentor before their relationship spectacularly deteriorated.

victims.name: Harry Houdini
victims.description: Escape artist, illusionist, and relentless enemy of fraudulent spiritualists.

comments.crowley: Houdini's crusade against supernatural fraud makes him an irresistible target for occult nonsense.

victims.name: Pierre Curie
victims.description: Physicist, researcher, and one half of an extraordinarily radioactive marriage.

comments.curie: Pierre was Marie Curie's husband and scientific collaborator.

victims.name: Henri Becquerel
victims.description: Physicist who discovered spontaneous radioactivity and thereby gave everyone considerably more work.

comments.curie: Becquerel's discovery directly preceded and influenced the Curies' research into radioactivity.

victims.name: Paul Langevin
victims.description: French physicist whose private life became significantly more public than intended.

comments.curie: Curie's relationship with Langevin became the center of a major public scandal.

victims.name: Albert Einstein
victims.description: Theoretical physicist, professional hair icon, and eventually the default visual shorthand for genius.

comments.curie: Einstein was a friend and supporter of Curie, particularly during the Langevin scandal.

victims.name: George Soper
victims.description: Sanitary engineer and epidemiological investigator with a talent for finding people who did not want to be found.

comments.mallon: Soper identified Mary Mallon as the likely source of multiple typhoid outbreaks and confronted her about it.

victims.name: Sara Josephine Baker
victims.description: Physician and public-health reformer who specialized in solving problems people preferred to ignore.

comments.mallon: Baker participated in the effort to apprehend Mallon after she refused voluntary testing.

victims.name: Robert Koch
victims.description: Physician and microbiologist who helped establish that specific microorganisms cause specific diseases.

comments.mallon: Germ theory is doing Mallon's legal defense absolutely no favors.

victims.name: Louis Pasteur
victims.description: Chemist and microbiologist responsible for several discoveries inconvenient to anyone denying germs exist.

comments.mallon: Pasteur helped establish germ theory. Mallon would probably prefer everyone stop establishing it.

victims.name: John Snow
victims.description: Physician who tracked a cholera outbreak to contaminated water using suspiciously competent epidemiology.

comments.mallon: Snow helped establish the investigative methods that would later make asymptomatic carriers very uncomfortable.

victims.name: Arthur Wellesley, Duke of Wellington
victims.description: British commander, statesman, and owner of one extremely inconvenient Belgian victory.

comments.napoleon: Wellington commanded the Allied army that defeated Napoleon at Waterloo.

victims.name: Horatio Nelson
victims.description: British admiral with one arm, one eye, and an irritating habit of defeating the French.

comments.napoleon: Nelson destroyed Napoleon's hopes of challenging British naval dominance at Trafalgar.

victims.name: Tsar Alexander I
victims.description: Emperor of Russia and owner of a country Napoleon discovered was considerably larger than expected.

comments.napoleon: Alexander opposed Napoleon and survived the 1812 invasion of Russia considerably better than Napoleon did.

victims.name: Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher
victims.description: Prussian field marshal who considered seventy-two an entirely reasonable age to keep ruining Napoleon's day.

comments.napoleon: Blücher's Prussian forces arrived at Waterloo and helped turn Napoleon's defeat into a catastrophe.

victims.name: Ludwig van Beethoven
victims.description: Composer, pianist, musical revolutionary, and famously difficult man to impress.

comments.napoleon: Beethoven initially admired Napoleon, then angrily rejected him after Napoleon declared himself emperor.

victims.name: Sigmund Freud
victims.description: Neurologist and founder of psychoanalysis. In this building, he has made a catastrophic career choice.

comments.rasputin: Freud would undoubtedly have questions. Rasputin would undoubtedly hate all of them.
comments.crowley: There are several possible interpretations of Crowley. Freud should keep them to himself.

victims.name: Nikola Tesla
victims.description: Inventor, electrical engineer, futurist, and magnet for increasingly implausible legends.

comments.curie: Different fields, same general period, approximately enough electricity and radiation to make everyone nervous.

victims.name: Florence Nightingale
victims.description: Nurse, statistician, reformer, and dangerous advocate for cleanliness.

comments.mallon: Nightingale's obsession with sanitation puts her philosophically on the worst possible side of this dispute.

victims.name: Queen Victoria
victims.description: Queen of the United Kingdom, Empress of India, and unwilling namesake of an entire century's furniture.

comments.napoleon: Wrong generation of Bonaparte, but Napoleon has never respected borders and apparently now rejects time.
comments.crowley: Crowley was born during Victoria's reign. This is apparently enough.

victims.name: Edgar Allan Poe
victims.description: Writer, poet, critic, and suspiciously appropriate person to find dead in an asylum.

comments.crowley: No meaningful connection is required. Look at the man.

victims.name: Oscar Wilde
victims.description: Writer, wit, aesthete, and almost certainly the person with the best last words in the room.

comments.crowley: Their timelines overlap just enough for the asylum to insist this makes sense.

victims.name: Charles Darwin
victims.description: Naturalist whose observations about finches eventually caused arguments about practically everything.
